YESKAMO Solar Security Camera Wireless - Outdoor Rechargeable Battery WiFi Camera, 1080P HD Video Solar Powered IP Cameras for Home Security, Wire Free 2 Way Audio Surveillance System ***SEE 2022 UPDATE AT THE BOTTOM OF REVIEW***
This is an excellent security camera. It was very easy to set up and I love the fact it’s truly wireless. The picture quality (both day and night) is great. There is an app that you download to your phone that is easy to use. If you wish to share on multiple phones, you each need to create your own account and can share from then on. The only thing that could have been improved is the SD card slot. Normally, you get a bounce back feature (if you push the card in it pops out), this didn’t have that. If I want to retrieve the SD card I will probably have to do so with a pair of tweezers. Also, it doesn’t tell you which way too insert the SD card. It would be nice if it had this in the directions. Overall it’s still an excellent product.

Update to review: We love this camera so much that we ordered 2 more!! 😃

2022 update to review: We purchased a 5th camera because we loved the others so much. This one records in high quality, however the only difference is that you have to use a completely different app than the other 3 cameras. It appears that in 2022 there was an update with these cameras and the old app is not compatible with the new cameras. Just an FYI if you buy these (if you have the previous version of this camera)!

Until we moved to a new house. The arris modem was dropping signal significantly every single day - we either had super slow or no connection for hours. I had the cable guys out here four times in 61 days to fix the problem. I was literally ready to just cancel Suddenlink and move to AT&T for internet, but decided to try this Nighthawk combo first.

It was spotted instantly by Suddenlink when I called to give them the new modem Mac address, so the connection was just a single phone call to start. No drama. I have 9 daily devices on WiFi and three TiVo receivers that connect via Ethernet or WiFi plus the land line phone. There's four Ethernet connections and two phone connections on the modem, plenty for our needs.

It's been almost three weeks and I've noticed an astonishing improvement in our initial connection and reliability. Rather than daily outages, we have had five total in three weeks and none lasted more than 15 to 20 minutes. Stability of the signal has improved and our speeds are double what they were with the arris modem - we're actually getting the high speed service we pay for. The router is also projecting the WiFi far enough that I no longer need to use a secondary extender to get WiFi by the pool and patio.

I like the Genie app with this. The ability to check channels, reboot the router if needed, and see which devices are online is very handy. I also like the clear, bright lights on the front. At a glance you know if there's a problem. Bottom line for me is that I haven't canceled our services from Suddenlink because this unit fixed 90% of our problem.

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag There is always a run on headphones in our house. Not only are they being lost or dying, but everyone is on a constant quest for the best design and sound they can find in a bluetooth headphone. Let's see how these measure up.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
These headphones have a long sturdy neck band which means they will fit a variety of neck sizes. Each ear piece has a magnet on it so that when you are not using them, they will close in front of you so you won't lose them. The controls are at the end of the neck band on the right side.

ON/OFF BUTTON
Play, pause, on/off, pair can be done with this button.

VOLUME
The minus and plus of volume control is also used for skipping songs- + skip forward, - skip backward.

ANC
There is an ANC button on the right side directly behind the negative volume button which makes it easy to press them both at the same time. It does do noise canceling, but it is frustrating because it is easy to press the ANC button by mistake when also pressing the middle button.

CHARGING PORT
Charging port is on the edge of the control button area.

AI INDICATOR VOICE
The automatic voice is very dysfunctional. It only says part of words, and seems to be a bit mean sounding which makes my daughter say it feels creepy.

NOISE CANCELING
The noise canceling works beautifully on these headphones.

SOUND QUALITY
The sound quality is awesome. Highs and mids are where they should be. Bass is very good. It is not overdone but it is in balance and does not distract from the music. There are not any breakups in sound unless you walk away from the device.

BLUETOOTH RANGE
The bluetooth range seems to be good up to about 35 feet or so.

PHONE CALL QUALITY
The calls go through very well and people can hear just fine on phone calls.

BATTERY PERCENTAGE
There is no physical light indicator to tell you how much battery power you have left.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want a good solid set of headphones to use with phone and music that work well, are in balance, and great for listening. The controls are not as convenient as they could be, which can be frustrating at times.

MY RATING
Four stars. If the control area was set up just a little more conveniently so that you can not accidentally press the wrong buttons all of the time, they would probably be five stars.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Neckband Headset Bluetooth V4.2 in-Ear Waterproof Earbuds Magnetic Hi-Fi Stereo Sports Earphones with Mic, Carrying Bag

GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only I love GL.iNet. They create routers based on OpenWRT, which has so many great features that you'd find in professional level routers that cost thousands of dollars. There is a fairly steep learning curve to it, though. Fortunately, GL.iNet understands this and makes things easier by creating their own customizations to the firmware to make OpenWRT easier to use and more custom to the routers themselves.

The GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) is their latest 4G LTE router. Pop in a sim card and the router will create a hotspot that routes to the LTE network. For additional protection, it is easy to set up the router to connect to a VPN provider. By connecting the router to VPN, all client computers connecting to it WIFI will be protected.

I used this router during my last trip and it was GREAT. I have a few devices that I bring with me. A laptop, tablet, and phone. I even bring a firetv with me sometimes. While in the car, I have the router connecting everyone's devices to the Internet via LTE and when I got to the hotel, I connected the router to the hotel's wifi and turned on VPN. The transition from LTE to hotel wifi was seamless. Not only did I not need to reconfigure everyone's devices to connect to the hotel WIFI, we were also secure behind the router's firewall and VPN connection.

The two restrictions that this product may present to potential buyers is first, the price. It is quite pricey and it can be hard to justify its purchase. Especially when you can get a travel router for around $40 with the ability to tether a phone via USB. The second issue is that this specific router is tied down to the T-Mobile network with no ability to unlock it for other networks (according to the seller's response in the questions section of for this product). If the convenience and the ability to fully control the TTL to bypass t-mobile's tethering throttling restrictions is important to you, it may justify the price you'd be paying.
text_fidelity_b: GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only

I wanted a second charger for another location. The EasyStyle SK90B195462looks like the original but is much lighter, probably due to being a switching power supply. My laptop had been discharged down to 5% prior to plugging the replacement charger in. The connector fit fine, but the laptop did not recognize the charger and warned that it may not work. I figured that's just Dell telling me it's not a Dell accessory. I permanently shut off the warning (an option) and continued to use the EasyStyle charger. Charging appeared normal and battery status was indicated as charging. However, after a short while it seemed stuck at 11% charge. I came back a few hours later and it was still indicating at 11%. I plugged in the Dell charger and 100% full charge was indicated immediately. I unplugged the Dell charger and the computer still indicated nearly full charge. I plugged in the new EasyStyle charger and the indication was charging and still near full charge.
My conclusion is that the charger works, but may cause the computer to give incorrect charge status under some conditions and it will be best to unplug the charger to get an accurate battery status.

ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White Update Jan 2016: After only a few months of use, the modem started acting up. At first, a reboot would cure the problem, but it got progressively worse whereas I needed to reboot it every few hours. It then failed to work at all even though all the indicator lights were indicating it was functioning properly. Swapped it with a different modem and all the problems went away.

Normally I would not down rate an item because of a failure since everything can break. However, if you expect to get warranty support for this, forget it. Arris/Motorola will not stand behind their product at all.

If you're OK with this being disposable when it breaks, go for it. It did work well when it was working. But, if you expect to get warranty support/repair/replacement, go for another brand.

Original review:
So far this has been a champ in terms of performance. I'm using it with Cox, and it replaces another DOCSIS 3.0 modem I had been using for the past four years (a Motorola SB6120). I got it mainly because I was concerned that my old modem would eventually die on me, and wanted to have a backup.

Installation was simple (just a quick call to Cox to give them the MAC id and serial number). Connection speeds have been slightly better than the SB6120 and more consistent. This seems to run no warmer than the SB6120, which is to say it's pretty warm but not hot when operating. The indicator lights are brighter on this model which, for me, is not a problem given where I have the modem located, but could be an issue if you have your modem out in the open -- the lights are beacon-bright in a dark room.

I'm hoping to get the same solid, dependable performance out of this that my SB6120 gave me. I'll update the review should reliability prove to be a problem down the road. But, at present, this is performing perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White

text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV If you read the product description carefully, you won't waste time (as I did) trying to use this PLAYSTATION 4 UNIVERSAL MEDIA REMOTE to navigate PS4 games (e.g., Journey, Minecraft). The PS4 remote uses Bluetooth to turn your PS4 on and off, and to control and navigate PS4 media (e.g., DVDs), but only controls PS4 media. The PS4 remote can also be programmed to turn your TV, Cable Box, and Audio Receiver on and off, and to control and navigate those devices (assuming they accept remote Bluetooth operation).

The PS4 remote performs the advertised functions very well, and I'm happy with it. The main thing I wanted was the PS4 on/off feature, so that I wouldn't have to fool with the skinny button on the PS4 box when I wanted to play a DVD. But I also wanted something that would make it easier to navigate DVDs. I'm not much of a gamer, and I find the game controllers awkward to use. With the PS4 remote, the forward, back, play, and arrow buttons work "normally" (like any TV remote).

NOTE THAT once the PS4 remote is paired, you will turn the playstation "on" by pressing the big PS4 button, but you will turn it "off" by navigating to the PS4's power settings (in the display). (The PS4 remote doesn't have a "sources" button for bringing up the output options on my Samsung Smart TV, so I still need a second remote for selecting the PS4 output.)

The Bluetooth pairing and setup for the PS4 remote is straightforward, but you need to follow the directions in the accompanying booklet "to the letter". You have to visit several locations in the PS4 settings to add the remote to the PS4 device list, and then complete the setup.

Programming the remote to turn on another device (TV, Cable Box, Amplifier, etc.) is exactly the same as programming any universal remote. You turn on the device you're programming, put the remote into learning mode, point it at the device, and wait for the remote to find, recognize, and turn off the device. If the remote doesn't recognize the device, you must perform the device code programming manually (lots of codes are listed in the instruction booklet). The PS4 remote recognized my TV without difficulty, but my sound bar required manual programming.

Once you've programmed the various other devices, you switch between those devices by pressing the little labeled buttons (PS4, TV, AMP, CBL). Which brings me to the only thing that I don't like about the PS4 remote--the buttons (especially the switching buttons) are quite small, because there are so many of them packed onto this rather narrow remote.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

There is one minor disadvantage, other than what seems to be a tad pricey - the bulk of the unit. It is difficult to place this in plug points with tight corners or abutting walls. This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. This is not a huge problem, but I'll certainly miss that since the case for my original Fire has a outside pouch that is great for holding a cleaning cloth and a small stylus.

I'm going to give this 5 stars, but 4.5 is more accurate given the reluctance of the rotation feature. But, since it does everything else very well, looks good, and feels nice, it's closer to a 5 rating than a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models)

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy.

Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear.

I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars.

Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store.

Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display

Kidz Gear Wired Headphones for Kids - Ltd. Edition White Great headphones at a great price. These fit my little man very well, and they are so adjustable even I could put them on to check out the volume.

I'm impressed by the sound quality, especially for this price.

My ONE complaint is that the sound limiter is a separate piece AND this is not clearly marked anywhere on the packaging. I used it for a few weeks before I knew the volume wasn't limited on his precious little ears, it was in an Amazon review that I found out I actually had to retrieve that from the spare part box and use it. I'd thought it was an adapter for other size jacks or soothing. There are no instructions or info booklets in the box, so if you give these as a gift, let the recipient know that volume limiter is separate. Since these are for kids, I don't understand why they don't just limit the volume on the headset itself. Or at the very least, find a way to plug it that holds more tenaciously (like a built-in tie from the headphone to the limiter). That tiny piece is fascinating for kids to remove and easy to lose.

This product is brand new for DLINK and the iOS app felt like a 1.0 product. The iOS app did get an update during my testing but it’s still a bit crashy and does not offer as many features as the web interface. Hopefully there will be more firmware updates.

Pros
- Units are small and unassuming
- Allow you to disable the bright white lights (warning lights will still function).
- Supports multiple connected devices (over 30 WiFi enabled devices) without issue.

Cons
- Primary access point needs to be rebooted (it seems like once a week) as it loses access to the Management interface (via the Web Page and App).
- Comes with different color faceplates for the access points (Metalic Blue and Copper) but it only comes with one of each color. If you want to change the color of the other access points you need to purchase two more faceplates.
- Product is still new. Other more refined products on the market from NetGear, Linksys and Eero.

The results are phenomenal. I'm now booting up in 20-30 seconds instead of 2-3 minutes. Programs like Word and Excel come up so fast (without any associated services running full time in the background) that you barely see the splash screen. I firmly believe a good SSD is the best thing you can do for a computer. 250GB seems to be the sweet spot right now as far as price goes (i.e., a similar 500GB drive will probably cost more than twice as much).

When cloning the a larger drive, you have to drag and drop all the smaller partitions over first, and then your C partition, which is probably your largest and with the most empty space. The program will then chop off the extra free space on the C partition, which is fine. Otherwise, you will lose any partitions logically after the C partition.

text_fidelity_a:
Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.
text_fidelity_b: Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications My husband put this on one of the farm Polaris CUV's since installation is beyond what I would able to do. He was able to install it on a ranger using the roof system as the mounting position for the speakers. It installed easily enough - basically clamp the speaker to the roof support bars, make sure to use the included rubber strips to get these to clamp securely or you will be remounting these with the rubber strips again once they slide down. Wiring was simple as it all goes to one plug that attaches to the amp. This does mean you will be mounting all 4 speakers. And since the wiring is together in a harness, some thought is required as to where you put the speakers and a good route to where you want the amp installed. The amp install is simple as it basically needs power (12vdc) and not a lot else. It does come with a handy audio input jack so you can use something like an old iPod for audio input. It also has BNC inputs if you have say a radio that you would want to connect to it so there is some flexibility there. The Bluetooth hook up was simple and works well, but again do not hide the amp behind a lot of metal or this may not work to well.

As far as fit and finish, the only thing I can knock this on is the quality of the clamping hardware finish, but being on a rough duty vehicle this is actually okay.

The bottom line is: Overall installation is simple, and the unit is easy to use.
text_fidelity_b: Sound Storm Labs SMC90BB Sound System Weatherproof Bluetooth Amplifier 3 Inch Speakers Inline Volume Control Ideal for Motorcycles ATV and 12 Volt Applications

Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery I selected this keyboard after doing a bit of research. I already have a solar keyboard (a Logitech) on my Windows system, and I needed a keyboard for my Linux system. I was a little hesitant to buy because I did not see any definitive information that it would work with Linux. I've had it several days, and I can say with some authority, it definitely works correctly under Linux.

The system in question is a Dell laptop running Peppermint Linux hosting a CentOS 8 VM. Most keyboards (with one notable exception) work on this system so I was hopeful it would work well, and it does. It behaves virtually identically to the Logitech keyboard and so far has given me no trouble.

Build-wise, this is a solid keyboard that should hold up to some abuse. It is sturdy and does not flex when I am typing. I like the fact that the dongle is held to the back of the keyboard magnetically so it can be transported with less concern of being misplaced when not in use.

One of the major issues I have with keyboards is that I have the hands of a gorilla and I frequently run into issues with hitting multiple keys at the same time, particularly with flat keyboards like this one. The keys are slightly bigger than average with this one, though, and hitting muliple keys simultaneously is less of a problem. This was an unexpected and welcome surprise.

Aesthetically, I love the feel of this keyboard. Most of the keys are concave and feel pleasant to the touch. Oddly, a good number of the keys on the bottom row are actually convex. While this is no issue at all, I do find it puzzling.

It is priced competitively against the Logitech too.

If I could change anything I would include some kind of indicator of how much charge this keyboard has at any given time. So far I have not run out of power, but eventually I expect to have a situation where there has not been enough light to keep it at a full charge and it would be good to know how much power it has retained.

I'm pleased with this keyboard. It works well under Linux and I don't need to replace batteries or plug it in. I really can't ask for much more than that.
text_fidelity_b: Arteck Wireless Solar Keyboard Full Size Solar Recharging Keyboard for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop/Surface/Smart TV and Windows 10/8 / 7 / Vista/XP Built in Rechargeable Battery

Camera Tripod Handle for Big Cam - MT- 43 Portable Sturdy Travel Vlog-Style Tripod Small Tabletop Acra Swiss QR Ballhead Tripod Extendable Cold Shoe Handheld for Heavy Camera Mirrors DSLR Digital I mostly like this tripod. It is solidly built and has a lot of useful features, but it also has some shortcomings that prevent me from giving it 5 stars. Here are my most important plusses and minuses:

Plusses:
+ precise construction
+ important components are sturdy metal, especially the ball head and the locking mechanisms that control the center post and the legs
+ folds up compactly for easy travel
+ relatively lightweight compared to solid metal tripods
+ cold shoe is very useful for attaching a microphone or video light

Minuses:
- legs only fold out in one flat position, so this tripod can really only be used on flat level surfaces (like tabletops).
- center post cannot be pushed all the way down below the legs like with most tripods for maximum stability
- selfie-stick mode is only 12 inches long maximum
- $80 price is expensive for a tabletop-only mini-tripod
text_fidelity_b: Camera Tripod Handle for Big Cam - MT- 43 Portable Sturdy Travel Vlog-Style Tripod Small Tabletop Acra Swiss QR Ballhead Tripod Extendable Cold Shoe Handheld for Heavy Camera Mirrors DSLR Digital

What I had big problems with, and which took hours of struggle to figure out and try to resolve:

I like the idea a lot if you're keeping this in a purse or a pocket with a bunch of other stuff, but I've long ago reserved an entire pocket for my phone. In the case of a pocket, all this added texture actually makes it harder to get the phone out. And I can see the drawback others' mention about it not keeping itself shut; this could be a problem in the case of a purse with keys and all kinds of junk rolling around in there.

I really like the materials, however, to include the thin metal backing and the faux leather front. It stands up fine for a phone, but when you're already adding this amount of thickness, it seems like you could build some stopping points into the inside front cover. Of course that would mess up the credit card pocket. And speaking of that pocket, it seems like a good idea, if you can refrain from cramming so much into it that your phone becomes your wallet. I have another pocket on most pants, which I reserve for my wallet and keys; makes me wonder how other people live in such disorganization.

It's a pretty good quality product, and I suspect if you're looking for a folio case, you won't find one better. However, the point of the cover not staying shut is valid and maybe a reason to continue your research.
text_fidelity_b: Incipio Highland Folio Case for Fire Phone, Black

Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.
text_fidelity_b: Webcam HD 1080p Web Camera, USB PC Computer Webcam with Microphone, Laptop Desktop Full HD Camera Video Webcam 110 Degree Widescreen, Pro Streaming Webcam for Recording, Calling, Conferencing, Gaming

Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker I've been relying on a cordless phone system with built-in call blocking, but it only stores 30 numbers. That gets filled up in short order, and I delete them and start over. I needed something better.

And this is definitely better. I'm using it with a cable-provided phone line and cordless phone system. And it works. Mostly.

The cool thing about this system is it intercepts everything by default, and announces that if the caller is a telemarketer, to remove us from their call list. It also announces that the caller can press "0" for the call to go through. This eliminates all robocalls, and most other unsolicited calls.

After the phone number is in the device's caller ID memory, you can then whitelist or blacklist it if you choose. Whitelisted numbers go straight through without an announcement and ring the phone normally. Blacklisted numbers are simply blocked. You might hear a partial ring, but that's the end of it.

There are a couple of down sides. When a caller presses "0", only the ringer in the device itself rings. It does not ring the phone system. If you're not near the room where the device is, chances are you won't hear it. So if you're expecting important calls, it's probably best to set the device to "off" when you're not within earshot of it.

And the other is -- and this may be a fault in the particular unit I received -- the "off" position is not always reliable. More than once it has continued to block calls when set to "off." If a really important call is expected, I'll probably just disconnect the unit from the phone system completely.

Other than that, it's effective. It blocks unwanted calls.
text_fidelity_b: SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker

SUDOKEJI 1000W Pure Sine Wave Inverter Power Inverter Peak Power 2000W 12V DC to 110V 120V AC with LED Display 3 AC Outlets & USB Port for RV Truck Boat This worked just fine for powering a few small items. When choosing what you are going to run on this add up the total wattage of all devices, then add at least 50% more to account for peaks or spikes in the power draw. For example if your coffee maker draws 500 watts, your laptop 300 watts, and your toaster 200 watts (total, 1000 watts) you should account for the extra 50% (1000watts + 500 watts (the 50%)=1500watts). In this example, a minimum 1500 watt inverter should be used.

If the item is motor driven, it requires additional start-up (surge) wattage (typically 2-3 times the continuous wattage required) to start the device. For example, a miter saw that runs at 700 watts might require 1400 watts to start up. If your inverter only supplies 1000 watts, you will not be able to start it up. In this case, you would want to select an inverter rated at least 1400 surge watts to handle start-up needs.

I understand how wattage works and for someone who doesn't, any inverter could fail if overloaded with more power than it can handle. An overload feature that automatically shuts the device off would be helpful for anyone who is unsure. This has an overload feature, but if you blow a fuse, you'll have to replace it. Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue) The LAP PRO universal tablet stand doesn't work very well with my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Wi-Fi tablet. The stand consists of a very firm, 18-inch wide, cylindrical pillow with a soft handle that doubles as a sort of tray for the tablet. Because there is no frame to hold the tablet securely, the tablet must be set carefully into the handle-tray, and then the tablet simply leans against the pillow for support. However, the tablet is very easily dislodged from the tray, even when the stand is sitting on a flat tabletop.

Out of the box, the LAP PRO holds the 8.9" Kindle Fire HD tablet at a near-vertical angle that is uncomfortable for viewing or for using a stylus on the touch screen. There is a sheet packed with the pillow that says: "Your LAP PRO has come slightly over filled intentionally, which may interfere with some functions. This will change in time. This is to ensure it will perform properly and last longer after it breaks in. The fabric will stretch and the beans settle from use." However, this is not really a beanbag stand. The pillow is filled with something that feels like medium-fine sand (not beans). Also, the pillow is too firm to accommodate its shape to an uneven surface the way a beanbag does.

To adjust the tablet viewing angle, you must reshape the pillow--it isn't enough to simply roll the pillow forward or backwards. Because the pillow is so firm, you must exert some effort in reshaping. It is easier to adjust the pillow shape and the viewing angle if you unzip the zipper that runs alongside the handle-tray, but then the pillow kind of flops around. (The zipper is there to open and close a compartment that is probably intended to hold your tablet, because the LAP PRO is also supposed to be a "caddy".)

If I needed a travel pillow (another of the LAP PRO's advertised uses) or a tablet caddy, I might end up liking the LAP PRO. However, because the stand is too large for convenient tabletop use, is hard to adjust, doesn't hold the tablet securely, and needs break-in time, I rate it at 2 stars ("I don't like it" on the official Amazon scale).

EDITED 11/18/12: After hearing from the seller, Renegade Concepts, I believe that I may have received an overfilled LAP PRO. (Renegade Concepts offered to replace my unit.) If my LAP PRO had been less firm out of the box, I would have rated it at 3 stars ("It's OK").
text_fidelity_b: Renegade Concepts: Lap PRO - Stand/Caddy Universal Beanbag Lap Stand Tablet Accessory for iPad 1, iPad 2, iPad 3, iPad 4, Acer, Nexus & All Android Tablets, E-Readers, Books & Google Devices (Blue)

VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model) 7 May 2014: Thanks to Google's omission of full USB OTG function, file transfers are frustrating & sometimes impossible. When I return home, I'm rooting it.

After 24 hours, I like it. It's a little different from my Galaxy Player 5 inch. The extra processor speed is nice. So is the combination of the light weight and larger screen. The GP5 was getting bogged down by software bloat. It fits nicely in my old K3 case. So far, so good.

...and it works with my Targus Bluetooth keyboard. Actually, it works better than it does with the GP5. The Samsung has some key-mapping problems, probably due to Gingerbread.

As to reading, I happened to be starting a novel the other day, and started it on the Nexus 7. I had no problem. I did keep the brightness on 'Auto', so the light level of the screen matched the ambient light. With the GP5, matching light levels was a little chancy, so I had a bit more eyestrain. (Of course the extra 2" of screen have no bearing on that, right?)

I did try the freebie 'La Luna' video that Google gives away. It watched fine on the 7" screen. The thing I really like is that there is a 7" screen in the weight of a past-technology 5" package. I owned a Nook color for 13 days, but took it back because of the weight and balance. It just wasn't comfortable to hold.

I haven't tried any significant music listening. I suspect I'll still prefer my Clip+ for that. The Nexus is a little large for that purpose. I also haven't tried the camera in any particular serious way. A selfie and a picture of my cat isn't much of a trial. Again, I'll probably use a purpose-made camera for real pictures. I also haven't explored portability yet. In the case, it's a bit bulky for easy transport, whereas the GP5 fits in my pocket next to my cell phone. I probably won't put the N7 in my pocket without a case. It's a little large and fragile seeming for that.

...As to the camera, it's OK, the image quality is fine, but a 7" tablet just isn't a good ergonomic platform for picture taking. This is the best from an afternoon at Mass Audubon's Ipswich River Wildlife Sanctuary.

Picture is available at:
MobileRead Forums > E-Book Readers > Android Devices>Nexus 7 2013 1st Impressions

...And I still prefer my Clip+ for music. I hand to hunt around the Android store for a decent player for my collection which includes WMAs as well as MP3s. Google does not play WMAs (cue prissy, superior sniff). I settled on Poweramp, not because it was perfect, but because it was the first one I came to that was good enough. I just want to listen to some music, people, not commit my soul to a single, ringing, crystalline-pure music player that rules them all. Sheesh.

Someday I may do a better review, too. All of the usual things about tablets are at worst adequate on the N7.

Oh, one piece of free advice, worth every penny you paid: Don't go hog wild buying really great accessories. Shop around. A $3 wire easel from a craft store will make a fine desk stand. I have one at work and one at home. A chopstick and a binder clip will do in a pinch. Also, there are good $10 EVA zip cases that will protect your N7 for transport. They don't have to be purpose built. My old K3 had a case that loosely fits the N7 (freebie!) and my KPW1 lives in a similar case. As to ear buds, the candy-colored $5 ones in the bin at the cash register at WalGreens are my favorite, and you never misplace them, because candy-colored.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model)

MOMAX Portable 56” 1.87lbs Compact Aluminum Alloy Lightweight Camera Tripod Monopod with Swivel Head, 5.5 lbs Loads for Phone, Camera Sony Canon Nikon, Travelling, Learning and Working (Grey) The MOMAX Compact Aluminum Tripod is super compact, moderately sturdy, and fairly light-weight and I really love it.

I have three kinds of tripods, all consumer grade, nothing professional. As seen in my pictures, I compare the size of all three types. Farthest to the right is the standard tripod that doesn't fold down all that much, the middle is the compact tripod with a ball head and quick release, and the MOMAX is the farthest left.

From the pictures, you can see how much more compact the MOMAX tripod is. What you can't see is that due to its compact size, the footprint when fully deployed is also much smaller. It expands to a height of 56 inches, which is about chin or head height, which is tall enough for most portraits.

The MOMAX tripod is super portable while not compromising on stability and sturdiness. Its folded size is only 10.3" long and 3" in diameter. Compare this to my previous solution, which was to use a monopod/selfie stick with a small tripod at the bottom, this tripod is so much better. Mounting my mirrorless camera on the MOMAX, I don't worry about the whole thing falling over.

The only tiny complaint I have about this tripod is its mounting head. It is a ball joint with a 1/4" thread at the top. It can't be removed easily to be replaced with a better solution and there is no quick-release option.

Each of my tripods serve a purpose but I foresee using the MOMAX most often because most of the time.
text_fidelity_b: MOMAX Portable 56” 1.87lbs Compact Aluminum Alloy Lightweight Camera Tripod Monopod with Swivel Head, 5.5 lbs Loads for Phone, Camera Sony Canon Nikon, Travelling, Learning and Working (Grey)

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.

text_fidelity_a:
NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green) Although there are a lot of positive points to be said about this product, a major flaw with it is that - even on low volumes and on songs without much bass - you can hear a bit of distortion, like crackly static, that sounds like a speaker that you're either working too hard or is at the end of its life. This becomes worse as the battery gets low. I consider this issue to be "understandable and sort of acceptable" considering the whole system has to run on battery power and most people aren't expecting high power out of such a setup. They might just have a high-pass crossover set too high to conserve power, and too much is cut off, resulting in messy sound.

When you charge your phone with the speaker's battery (which in itself is sort of a nice, if cannibalistic, feature, one that other devices claim even though it is inherent to the device; with this, the USB-A port was added specifically for this purpose), it lowers the volume to level 8 (there is nothing to tell you what level you're at) to keep from draining the battery quickly. Even at this medium level and below, this problem can be recognized.

The bike mounts are 4" apart, center to center, so make sure you have room on your bike handlebars if that is your purpose for ordering. Included bike mounts are good. It also comes with a neoprene case, a USB cable, and an audio cable, both red. With all these extras trying to give the appearance of premium, it doesn't actually come with a charger, not that this will be an issue for most people (you probably already have more than you know what to do with).

There should be keyhole slots built into the bike mounts so it could also be hung on the wall and removed easily, making it more versatile.

The unit pairs easily and immediately with my Blackberry every time, and it can control the tracks through the BT connection as well. It looks well made and has a good feel to it. It looks like it could almost be waterproof, although I noticed no mention or claim of that feature (so I'm sure it's not).

The sound overall isn't bad for a low voltage battery operated speaker, as long as you're not sitting down and listening too closely. I guess for the purposes of making noise as you ride around the neighborhood, it'll do just fine.
text_fidelity_b: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)

iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things.

Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most.

I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet.

Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.
text_fidelity_b: iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp
